title: the running Krita session
instructions: Commands run inside the open Krita. 'docs' lists open documents; 'layers' lists every layer and mask of every open document, inside groups too, as JSON lines with an id and a DOC/Group/Layer path (unsaved documents go by their name, or #N when it is not unique). 'layer set' edits many layers at once. 'filter' finds and applies any of Krita's filters, with their parameters checked against the defaults (filter ls, filter info, filter apply). 'open' and 'save' handle files (save DOC PATH: .kra saves as, other formats export); 'view' saves a PNG of a document and prints its path, so you can look at the result. 'python' runs one-off Python inside Krita, from stdin (`from krita import *` is done, app = Krita.instance()). Commands that take layers read ids or paths from arguments or stdin, so they chain: layers | jq -c 'select(.kind=="vectorlayer")' | layer set visible false. Values are checked before anything changes. Krita's scripting API records no undo steps, so edits cannot be undone with Ctrl+Z: prefer 'filter apply --mask' (a removable filter mask) over baking a filter in, and confirm with the user before modifying their documents.
setup:
1. Install the Krita plug-in: mcp_sh_krita plugin install (Krita 5.2+; start Krita once first so its resource folder exists).
2. In Krita: Settings > Configure Krita > Python Plugin Manager, enable "mcp-sh-krita Bridge", then restart Krita. The bridge starts with Krita from then on.
Check with: mcp_sh_krita commands
The bridge listens on 127.0.0.1:9530 with no token; to change either, set {"port": N, "token": "..."} in ~/.mcp-sh/krita/bridge.json and MCP_SH_KRITA_PORT / MCP_SH_KRITA_TOKEN for mcp-sh-krita, then use Tools > Scripts > Restart mcp-sh-krita Bridge.
Add a folder of your own Python commands with: mcp_sh_krita commands add PATH

host.hint: enable the bridge in Krita: Settings > Configure Krita > Python Plugin Manager > mcp-sh-krita Bridge, then restart Krita (install it with 'mcp_sh_krita plugin install')
